The docs use "rest at the inn" as their own worked example. ## Worker | File | Change | |---|---| | `worker/src/types/index.ts` | Add `RestBody { sessionId: string; characterId: number }` next to the other `*Body` types (around `:146-168`). Add a cost constant such as `INN_REST_COST`. The cost could instead scale with level, but that is your call. | | `worker/src/routes/rest.ts` (new) | Export `restRoutes = new Hono<{ Bindings: Env }>()` with `POST /`. It should:
• Validate the body.
• Call `getCharacter`.
• Reject with 400 if `gold < cost`, if `hp === max_hp`, or if the session is in combat (the session's `CombatState` is set).
• Call `updateCharacter(db, id, { hp: max_hp, gold: gold - cost })`.
• Optionally call `askDM` for narration, then `appendHistory` and `saveSession`, and insert into `adventure_log`, following `routes/action.ts`.
• Return `{ narrative, updatedCharacter }`. | | `worker/src/index.ts:41-48` | Import `restRoutes` and add `app.route('/api/rest', restRoutes)`. No CORS change is needed because the origin is unchanged. | | `worker/src/services/character.ts:94` | Likely no change, since `updateCharacter` already accepts `hp` and `gold`. Confirm both are in its whitelist. | No schema change is needed because `hp`, `max_hp` and `gold` already exist, so there is no new migration. Put the cost and HP logic in the Worker, not the AI, because the Worker owns the rules. ## Frontend | File | Change | |---|---| | `frontend/src/app/models/game.models.ts` | Add a `RestResponse { narrative: string; updatedCharacter: Character }` interface mirroring the Worker response.
